Cc: ops@acme.com

Subject: Sudden RTT/p95 uplift for hosted API in us-west -> us-east traffic

Hi Laura —

We're seeing a large jump in p95/p99 latency for requests that originate from our us-west customers and are routed to the hosted inference endpoint. The dashboard spike starts ~07:45 PDT and shows p95 going from ~160ms to ~520ms and p99 into the 800–1,000ms range. Error rates have not materially increased, but tail latency is killing our client SLAs.

We've attached a small trace bundle and a screenshot of the p95 dashboard. Can Redwood confirm anything on your side? Our SREs suspect an inter-region routing adjacency change.

- Sudhir
Platform Ops | Acme Corp

Attachments: support_trace_20270621.zip (trace bundle), p95-dashboard.png (screenshot)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden RTT/p95 uplift for hosted API in us-west -> us-east traffic

Thanks — I've pulled the traces. Quick findings:

- The traces show hop-level RTT increases consistent with an extra inter-region hop for many traces originating in us-west.
- Control-plane config audit: a deploy at 07:35 PDT introduced a routing adjacency change in the mesh (route-map v2.14) that unintentionally preferred a us-east transit path for certain us-west edge nodes.
- No model-serving capacity issues observed on the us-east clusters; CPU/GPU and queue depths look normal. This is purely an added network path cost.

Immediate recommended actions:
1) Roll back route-map v2.14 to v2.13 on the edge-pop clusters that serve us-west (this will restore previous adjacency and eliminate the extra hop).
2) As a short-term safety net, configure a traffic-steering rule to prefer local-region pools for requests with us-west source regions.
3) Notify affected customers and offer to waive credits for the window 07:45–09:20 PDT.

Hannah/Sean — can you own the rollback + steer? I'll prepare a post-mortem blameless timeline once we stabilize.

-Rishi
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden RTT/p95 uplift for hosted API in us-west -> us-east traffic

Update / mitigation summary (11:14 PDT):

Actions taken:
- Rolled back route-map v2.14 -> v2.13 for the three affected edge-pop clusters serving us-west (rollback completed at 10:02 PDT).
- Applied a temporary traffic-steering rule (prefer-local-region) at 10:06 PDT for the us-west edge cohort; this forces local-region pools for requests marked with us-west geolocation.
- Observed p95 fall from ~520ms to ~170ms in the affected cohort over the 10:06–10:30 PDT window. p99 similarly reduced to ~300–350ms.

Customer communication:
- Laura, I drafted a note to Sudhir to confirm the fix and propose a credit for the affected window. See below.

Next steps:
- Rishi to lead a blameless post-mortem and identify CI/CD guardrails to prevent inadvertent adjacency promotes.
- Ops and Network to add a canary gate for route-map changes that impact region affinity.
- Prep a short status page entry for transparency.

— Hannah
Director, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference

Hi Sudhir —

Thanks for the report and for the traces. Short version: we found a control-plane routing adjacency change (route-map v2.14) that caused some us-west edge nodes to prefer a us-east transit path, which added an extra inter-region hop and increased tail latency.

What we did: Hannah rolled back the route-map and applied a prefer-local steering rule. You should see p95/p99 return to normal; our metrics show the window of impact from ~07:45–10:06 PDT. Attached are the traces we collected after remediation.

We'd like to offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window and schedule a 30-minute post-incident sync tomorrow to walk through the timeline and our proposed guardrails. Proposed time: Wed 2027-06-22 09:00 PDT. Please let me know if that works.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll share a short post-mortem and follow up on hardening steps (canary gate for route-map deploys, region-affinity tests).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachments: support_trace_20270621_fix-logs.zip (post-rollout traces)
